notes: Logo: none. The site header shows the business name as text only. The only logo-like files are certification badges (Eco Certified, Tourism Council of WA, COVID Clean, Sustainable, ECOSTAR) and a site icon at https://ningalooblue.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/cropped-icon-1.png that was not checked, so logo is null. Hero: no heroImage given; the facts file uses the site's own header photo (2021/01/shark.jpg, also its social share image). No photos were opened or downloaded, so content was judged from page position and file names only, and every URL was confirmed with a header request (all answered as image/jpeg); a person should look at shark.jpg and the gallery before publishing. Every photo is the original upload, not a sized copy, and not the Jetpack CDN copy. Trip photos: the site has one tour page with one photo, so the trip list leads with that photo, then the home page's tour photos and a few whale shark photos from the gallery and wildlife pages. Gallery: whale shark and reef photos from the gallery, home and wildlife pages, plus two photos from the humpback section of the wildlife page. RIGHTS CHECK: most tour photos have file names for Blue Media Exmouth and a named photographer (violetajbrosig), who the site calls its professional independent videographer and photographer. The site presents the photos as its own and gives no credit line, so they are included, but a person should confirm Ningaloo Blue has the right to use them. Left out as banners or graphics: the Eco Certified, Tourism Council, COVID Clean, Sustainable and ECOSTAR badges, the TripAdvisor logo, and the marine calendar image on the Wildlife page. Left out as screenshots: every Screen-Shot PNG on the Wildlife and Exmouth pages (emus, kangaroos, turtles, Exmouth sights). Left out as belonging to other businesses or photographers: the hotel, resort and holiday park images on the Exmouth page, the blue-media-weddings photos (a wedding photography business), the fuey-photography underwater photo, the emouth-bluemedia beach and friends photos, the dugong photo and the ningalooreef photos named for the Blue Media handle with no tour link, and the humpback calf PNG. Videos: from the YouTube channel 'Peter Mckissock (Ningaloo Blue Exmouth)', which the site's page markup links to (it is not a visible link on the pages); the channel lists eight videos, aged about 7 to 13 years, and six are recorded. Left out: 'Whale Shark Eating Krill' (not clearly from a Ningaloo Blue trip) and a one minute promo ('ws 1 min PROMO feb') that may carry text. No bot check, captcha or 403 was hit on the site or on YouTube. The Rezdy catalog on the Book Now page was not opened.
